maria.sales: Quick question — ACME Health asked whether the POC can be considered in-scope for their upcoming ISO audit. They specifically want tenant isolation + customer-managed KMS and an applicability statement. Can PS/security confirm what's feasible and any pricing impact?
chris-ps: Do they need Dedicated (reserved) or Private (VPC/on-prem)? Isolation guarantees differ. For Dedicated we can strongly isolate at infra layer; Private gives them full control of networking and KMS but provisioning takes longer.
maria.sales: They used the phrase 'in their audit boundary' so probably Private. Also want a short POC (1 month) for 3 engineers — asked if this increases cost materially.
sam-security: We can provide an ISMS applicability statement + control mapping for the POC. Need to clarify: will auditors expect our product to appear in their SoA, or just evidence (config, KMS proofs, network diagrams)? Also need confirmation on subprocessors and data flows.
chris-ps: If inclusion in their SoA is required we need legal sign-off and a contractual addendum. Pricing: Private POC will include infra + setup fees — rough ballpark for 1-month reserved POC with 3 seats is ~$12k (setup + infra). I'll follow up with a precise quote.
alex.eng: Technical note: we can enable tenant isolation + customer-managed keys. Example config (high level):
```yaml
deployment: private
vpc: true
kms: customer_managed
seats: 3
retention_days: 30
```
This will produce separate VPC subnets, dedicated instance pools and a dedicated KMS key tied to their account.
sam-security: We'll prepare the evidence pack: ISMS scope statement template, controls mapping (ISO->our controls), KMS key lifecycle docs, network isolation diagram, sample audit logs export. ETA for initial pack: 48-72h once we have PO details. For formal SoA inclusion it's a legal process ~5-7 business days. cc @linda.legal
maria.sales: Good — please call out exactly what auditors will ask re: "control ownership" vs "control implementation" and any subprocessors that remain shared. Also need the provisioning ETA to tell the customer.
sam-security: Auditors typically ask: who owns the control (customer vs vendor), how it's implemented, supporting evidence (config, logs, IAM policies), and change history. Subprocessors: list + contracts will be included.
linda.legal: If the customer insists on a formal acceptance into their SoA we'll need an MSA addendum. Happy to draft/review once we have their language.
chris-ps: Quote sent via DM to Maria. Provisioning ETA: Private POC ~10 business days after signed paperwork and keys exchanged. Dedicated ephemeral env could be ~3-4 business days but note residual multi-tenant services for some platform components.
maria.sales: Awesome, thanks everyone — I'll relay to ACME and ask whether they prefer speed (Dedicated ephemeral) or strict isolation (Private). Will follow up with their preference. :thumbsup:
